input.quote: 10.2 Vendor shall deliver all completed and in-process Deliverables for which Customer has paid or agrees to pay the applicable proportionate Fees. Vendor shall refund prepaid recurring Fees covering the period after termination, together with Fees paid for Services Customer cannot reasonably use because of Vendor's uncured breach.
input.rationale: Section 10 (Effect of Expiry or Termination) addresses only access cut-off (10.1), Deliverable delivery and refunds (10.2). There is no obligation on Vendor to return or export Customer Data, no transition-assistance commitment, and no deletion/certification timing anywhere in the Agreement (searches for "transition", "export" and "delet" return nothing relevant; Section 15 imposes no return duty, and Section 16.5 defers Customer Data to "Sections 11 and 15" where Section 11 does not exist). For a hosted-services agreement this leaves us with no exit path for our data, so the playbook clause is inserted as new Section 10.3: up to six months of transition assistance at Vendor's then-current rates, data return in a commonly used machine-readable format within thirty days, and certified deletion thereafter. The obligation binds Vendor only.

ops.text: 10.3 Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement or any Order Form for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty days, return or make available for download all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems, subject to routine backups and legal retention requirements, and certify such deletion in writing.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We added an orderly exit provision: up to six months of transition assistance at Vendor's then-current rates, return of Customer Data in a machine-readable format within thirty days, and certified deletion thereafter. Section 10 currently ends access and returns Deliverables but says nothing about getting our data back or migration help (and Section 16.5 cross-refers to a non-existent Section 11), so we cannot exit without this. If six months is difficult, we can accept ninety days of assistance with the same thirty-day data export.
proposal.summary: Insert Section 10.3 requiring transition assistance, Customer Data return in machine-readable format within 30 days, and certified deletion.
